description: Production-grade Rust-native trading engine with deterministic event-driven architecture
summary: The Rust-core / Python-control-plane split is the same pattern I keep reaching for in PenguPool and AgentOn Pocket: a fast, typed engine doing the heavy lifting while a thin orchestration layer stays readable and swappable. What sells it to me is the deterministic event-driven backbone with a message bus and cache you can actually inspect, so backtest and live share the same strategy code and you can trust the simulation instead of hand-waving about "close enough." For anyone building local-first agent or pipeline systems where observability and reproducibility matter more than raw throughput, the adapter model—drop in any REST or WebSocket feed and get a uniform event stream—is a clean template for composable data ingestion.
